_about: Test CLASS file — machine-readable source for the qa/ viewer pages and the automated runner. Covers BOARD-ARRANGE1: drag-to-arrange, stays-where-dropped, spawn-at-drop-point, per-game persistence, tidy-on-demand. The automated instances run against the ?demo=1 sandbox (no backend, no wallet) via qa/harness/board-arrange.cjs; the same harness replays scripted move files (qa/harness/moves/) as narrated demos with video.
title: Chip arrangement — hand-placed chips stay where dropped; layout only re-flows on demand

hard_assertions: drag-to-arrange within a chip's own zone moves it to the release point and flags it user-pinned (body.pin)
a pinned chip does not move through a sim re-excite (0px drift over settle)
a pinned chip does not move when other chips arrive/leave its zone or the board re-renders
an offered/picked chip spawns AT the drop point in the target zone, pinned
pinned arrangements restore after a page reload (localStorage per game, zone-local coords)
🧹 tidy clears every pin (bodies + storage) and the auto-layout re-flows as visible motion
pinned chips remain solid: arrivals take the whole collision separation and route around them
walls still clamp pinned chips — a resize never strands one off the felt
cross-zone drops still route to offer/pick/reject/withdraw semantics untouched
oracle.trace_shape: gesture → arrange (no socket send) vs gesture → offer (socket send + pending-spawn note) — an arrange must never emit a game message

instances.steps: Automated: node qa/harness/board-arrange.cjs — arrange a store chip (A1), re-excite (A2), foreign offer lands elsewhere (A3), offered chip spawns pinned at drop point (A4), reload restores (A5), tidy clears (A6).

instances.why_manual: HTML5 native drag (dragstart/drop/dragend) needs a real OS drag pipeline — headless synthetic events don't drive it faithfully
instances.steps:
1. Desktop, ring16, any game (or ?demo=1).
2. Mouse-drag one of your OWN store chips a short way within your own wedge and release — it must stay exactly there (no snap-back, no re-blob), cursor must NOT show 🚫 over your own wedge.
3. Drag it again onto empty felt near the hub edge of your wedge — releases just outside the walls snap back; releases inside stick.
4. Offer a chip to another account by mouse — the chip should appear in their basket where you dropped it.
5. 🧹 tidy — everything re-flows.

instances.why_manual: shelves + pins coexistence is a judgement call (pinned chips sit outside the shelf rows) — needs an eyeball on whether it reads as intentional
instances.steps:
1. Settings → Chip layout → shelves.
2. Arrange one chip by hand — it must hold its spot while the others shelve around it (they may overlap the pinned one: acceptable? judge).
3. Offer into a basket at a specific point — spawns there even in shelves mode.
4. Reload — the pinned chip restores; the rest re-shelve.

demo.what: scripted-move replay: the harness executes a JSON move script through the real gesture handlers and records video — 'playing a game from a script'
demo.vocabulary: arrange / offer / tidy / reload / pause — see the moves file header; extendable toward lock/sign for full-game katrun-style demos
